title: Lease state file (laptop, internal)
description: The lease CLI's state file, %USERPROFILE%\.agentspace\leases.json (D8, D21). Internal: it is not part of the lease contract, and no caller reads it. One record per lease, holding the lease document's fields with its state as stored (pending, ready, released or unsatisfiable; expired is derived when the record is read, never stored), plus the opaque name of the driver that placed it, which never reaches any output. From v0.10 a lease created with a plan also carries sized_for, as the lease document does, and plan, the plan document as parsed, which no output holds; the two come together, with driver, on every such record in every state, and on no other. Strict like the contract's output schemas: anchored patterns end with $(?!\n). Every member it shares with the lease document has lease.output.schema.json's pattern, except ssh.user, which is narrower. A file in which two records share an id is not valid, though this schema cannot refuse it. See docs/state.md.

reasons.description: Every reason that applies, each code at most once. plan_too_large is always the only reason.

driver.description: The opaque name of the driver that placed the lease, handed back to it on renew and release.

plan.description: The plan document the lease was created with, whole, as parsed and stored compactly: the record only, never any output, its model and effort recorded and never printed. Kept for D27's later use of model and effort, and read by no sizing. Present exactly when sized_for is. Its form is plan.input.schema.json's, whose $defs (plan, plan_turn, plan_story, plan_subagent, plan_name, plan_model, plan_effort) this schema copies word for word. null for the plan's name or a subagent's after is kept as parsed, and means absent. What no schema checks (a cycle in after, an after naming no subagent, names given twice, the file's size) was checked when the lease was created, and is not checked again here.

plan_source.description: Where the plan was read from, on a lease created with create --board --epic: the board, the card's ticket and the card's revision read. Present only with plan, which this schema checks; that create writes it on a board lease alone, never on a --plan file lease, is create's rule, which no schema can check, since a record does not say where its plan came from. Written once by create, kept by renew and release, printed by nothing, and never holding a token, a base URL or any of the receipt.

sized_for.description: What a lease created with a plan was sized for, as the lease document prints it: the plan's name when it has one, its busiest turn's name, and that turn's agents at once, its dev lead counted. On every record created with a plan, in every state, and on no other.

agents.description: The busiest turn's agents at once, 2 to 1025.

plan_source.description: A board plan's source: the board's ID, a lowercase UUID, the card's ticket and the card's revision at the read, each an integer from 1 to 9007199254740991. All three are required, and no other member is allowed.

plan.description: A plan document: an optional name, such as its epic's, and its turns in order.

name.description: The plan's name, printed as sized_for.plan. Null or absent means the plan has none.

turns.description: The plan's turns in order, 1 to 32.

plan_turn.description: A turn: its name, unique in the plan, its stories, which run at once, and its budget, if it has one.

budget_minutes.description: The turn's wall-clock budget in whole minutes, 1 to 960, from which a lease for this turn takes its TTL. Null or absent means the turn has none.

plan_story.description: A story: its name, unique in its turn, and its subagents. Its peak is counted from the subagents' after lists, never stated.

plan_subagent.description: A subagent: its name, unique in its story, its model and effort, and the subagents of the same story it starts after.

after.description: The names of the same story's subagents this one starts after, each once, at most 31. Null, absent or empty means it starts after none.

plan_name.description: A name in a plan, as given: 1 to 64 printable ASCII characters, not starting or ending with a space. Never trimmed or case-folded.

plan_model.description: A model, as given, such as Opus or Opus 5.5: 1 to 64 printable ASCII characters, not starting or ending with a space, as a name in a plan is. Never trimmed or case-folded, and never a list of names, so a new model needs no new version.

plan_effort.description: An effort, as given: 1 to 32 ASCII letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-', starting with a letter or digit. Never a list of names, so a new effort needs no new version.
